title: Mechanically translated — 119 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
Mechanically translated. 119 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/mechanical.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. 107 are checked case by case over a stated finite domain (by decide). 12 are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 3 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 131 pairs; the theorems fall into 99 strands, the largest of 16. Most binding: DR (16), M9 (5), dbl (2). 94 theorems name no definition of the file and stand on their own statement.

2 · Imports. Built on: address.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 3 files: src/proof/mechanical.lean, src/proof/address.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 119 sealed receipts fold to 31b8d7d9-571e-8741-9afa-61db1fd23ad1. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 6, 3, 2, 3, 6, 4). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: priorart.lean (18 observed, 10.44 expected, lift 1.72), address.lean (30 observed, 19.72 expected, lift 1.52), phenomena.lean (7 observed, 4.64 expected, lift 1.51). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 1.65 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 45.5% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.51; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.5. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 95155bc810f5 (2026-09-15), over 719 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. The Boolean rows are De Morgan's laws — Augustus De Morgan, 1847 — written in the arithmetic of {0,1}; the group rows are the additive group of Z/9. Both long prior. Searched 2026-09-04, terms "De Morgan's laws boolean algebra" and "additive group mod 9"; prior art found and credited. Credited per theorem: every_multiple_of_three_four_five_is_pythagorean — the 3-4-5 triangle, known in antiquity. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.
